sentences.en: In London right now, there are sold-out shows, huge crowds, and audible gasps.
sentences.zh: 此刻在伦敦，演出场场爆满，观众人山人海，不时发出惊叹声。

sentences.en: I thought, oh my God.
sentences.zh: 我心想，天哪。

sentences.en: We weren't going to miss this, having not seen it in a lifetime yet, so.
sentences.zh: 我们这辈子还没见过它，所以无论如何也不能错过。

sentences.en: A nationwide mania, really.
sentences.zh: 这真是一场全国性的狂热。

sentences.en: We're here on our honeymoon.
sentences.zh: 我们是来度蜜月的。

sentences.en: How hard was it to get tickets for your honeymoon?

sentences.en: Over a tapestry.
sentences.zh: 为了挂毯。

sentences.en: It changed British history, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它改变了英国的历史。

sentences.en: A very old and very long and very beloved tapestry that people cannot wait to see.
sentences.zh: 这是一幅非常古老、非常长且深受人们喜爱的挂毯，大家迫不及待地想一睹真容。

sentences.en: I got it because I'm staying at a really lovely hotel.
sentences.zh: 我能买到是因为我住的酒店真的很棒。

sentences.en: You're not one of the people who's paid like a thousand pounds a night to get access.
sentences.zh: 你不是那种花了一千英镑一晚来获得入场资格的人吧。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是，是，是，没错。

sentences.en: Don't tell anybody.
sentences.zh: 别告诉任何人。

sentences.en: I'll be poor and go without food for the next week.
sentences.zh: 下周我得穷得吃土了。

sentences.en: But it was worth it for that.
sentences.zh: 但为了看它，这一切都是值得的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Today, the story of the Bayou Tapestry, how it became central to British identity, why it
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲述巴约挂毯的故事，它是如何成为英国身份认同的核心，为什么它

sentences.en: remained outside of Britain for nearly 1,000 years, and its improbable but temporary return to the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 在近1000年的时间里一直流落在英国境外，以及它那不可思议但短暂的回归英国之旅。

sentences.en: My colleague, culture reporter Alex Marshall, tells The Epic Yarn.
sentences.zh: 我的同事，文化记者亚历克斯·马歇尔，将为您讲述这段“史诗般的纱线”。

sentences.en: It's Sunday, September 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月20日，星期日。

sentences.en: Alex Marshall, welcome to the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·马歇尔，欢迎来到周日版《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请，迈克尔。

sentences.en: So, Alex, correct me if I'm wrong here.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚历克斯，如果我说错了请纠正我。

sentences.en: Tapestries rarely take the world by storm.
sentences.zh: 挂毯很少能风靡全球。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure no tapestry before has ever taken the world by storm, although we should probably say this is not a case of a tapestry taking the world by storm.
sentences.zh: 我很确定以前从来没有挂毯风靡全球，尽管我们可能应该说，这并不是挂毯风靡全球的案例。

sentences.en: This is the case of an embroidery taking the world by storm.
sentences.zh: 这是一个刺绣作品风靡全球的案例。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: So, we're already splitting hairs here.
sentences.zh: 看来我们已经在抠字眼了。

sentences.en: Can you just help me understand the difference between a tapestry and an embroidery?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我理解一下挂毯和刺绣的区别吗？

sentences.en: I do think this is important to start with, because otherwise we will have the embroidery mafia chasing us both down, and they've got quite sharp pins.
sentences.zh: 我觉得从这里开始很有必要，否则刺绣界的“黑手党”会追着我们俩跑，而且他们的针尖可是很锋利的。

sentences.en: A tapestry is woven on a loom, and embroidery is stitched by hand.
sentences.zh: 挂毯是在织布机上织出来的，而刺绣是手工缝制的。

sentences.en: And what we're here to talk about today is, sadly, an embroidery that happens due to the fault of an 18th century French monk to be known to the world as the Bayou Tapestry.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我们今天要谈论的这件作品，由于一位18世纪法国僧侣的失误，被世人称为“巴约挂毯”。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to take that distinction and politely store it away, and proceed perhaps to keep referring to it as a tapestry, but we'll see.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我会接受这个区别并礼貌地记在心里，也许之后还会继续称它为挂毯，但我们走着瞧吧。

sentences.en: I think even the entire world does that, and given the British Museum is currently eulogizing
sentences.zh: 我想全世界都是这么叫的，而且考虑到大英博物馆目前正在向

sentences.en: to the entire world about this Bayou Tapestry, I think we should go with the terminology that the world knows it by, and take the risk.
sentences.zh: 全世界盛赞这幅巴约挂毯，我认为我们应该沿用世人熟知的称呼，冒个险也无妨。

sentences.en: Okay, yes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，没问题。

sentences.en: So, Alex, what is it that makes this embroidery, this tapestry, this piece of fabric so very special?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚历克斯，到底是什么让这件刺绣、这幅挂毯、这块布料如此特别？

sentences.en: How did it become the Mona Lisa of textiles?
sentences.zh: 它是如何成为纺织品界的《蒙娜丽莎》的？

sentences.en: I mean, take your pick of reasons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，理由多得数不清。

sentences.en: I mean, let's start just with the sheer scale of this thing.
sentences.zh: 我们先从它惊人的尺寸说起吧。

sentences.en: I mean, it is 220 feet long.
sentences.zh: 它长达220英尺（约67米）。

sentences.en: I mean, very few artifacts in the world at that length that could fit in a stadium.
sentences.zh: 世界上很少有文物能达到这个长度，甚至能装进体育场里。

sentences.en: They could wrap around the outside of a basketball court.
sentences.zh: 它们可以绕篮球场外围一圈。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's almost 1,000 years old.
sentences.zh: 它已经有近1000年的历史了。

sentences.en: It is still as vibrant and bright in its colors almost as the day it was made.
sentences.zh: 它的色彩依然鲜艳明亮，几乎和刚制作出来时一样。

sentences.en: Like, it hasn't been faded.
sentences.zh: 它几乎没有褪色。

sentences.en: It's filled with holes.
sentences.zh: 上面满是破洞。

sentences.en: It's got tears in it.
sentences.zh: 还有撕裂的痕迹。

sentences.en: It's been stained.
sentences.zh: 上面还有污渍。

sentences.en: And then it's up there for British people with the crown jewels, with Stonehenge.
sentences.zh: 对于英国人来说，它的地位堪比王冠上的珠宝和巨石阵。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The Bayou Tapestry is something so important we teach it at schools.
sentences.zh: 巴约挂毯非常重要，以至于我们在学校里都要学习它。

sentences.en: We force it down children's necks.
sentences.zh: 我们强迫孩子们去了解它。

sentences.en: And it is back for the first time since it was made.
sentences.zh: 这是它自制作以来首次回归。

sentences.en: And that, for British people, has almost set the country on fire.
sentences.zh: 对于英国人来说，这简直让整个国家都沸腾了。

sentences.en: Everyone's talking about it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在谈论它。

sentences.en: Everyone wants to see it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想亲眼看看。

sentences.en: It is the hottest ticket in town.
sentences.zh: 它是目前最热门的入场券。

sentences.en: I'm straining and struggling for an American point of reference because what you're describing is nearly 1,000 years old.
sentences.zh: 我正在努力寻找一个美国的参照物，因为你描述的东西有近1000年的历史了。

sentences.en: And as you've probably heard, we just celebrated our 250th anniversary.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能听说的，我们刚刚庆祝了建国250周年。

sentences.en: So we just cannot compete.
sentences.zh: 所以我们根本没法比。

sentences.en: I don't think you can.
sentences.zh: 我想确实没法比。

sentences.en: But the strangest thing is whenever British people have been trying to sum it up for me because they, despite my accent, weirdly assume I'm American when I say I work for the New
sentences.zh: 但最奇怪的是，每当英国人试图为我总结它时——尽管我有口音，但当我提到我在《纽约时报》工作时，他们奇怪地以为我是美国人——

sentences.en: York Times, they always go, it's like the Declaration of Independence to you.
sentences.zh: 他们总是说，它对你们来说就像《独立宣言》一样。

sentences.en: And then whenever I say that to an American, they go, yeah, no, we wouldn't all queue up for nine hours to get a ticket to see the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 然后每当我把这话告诉美国人时，他们就会说，不，我们才不会为了看《独立宣言》排九个小时的队呢。

sentences.en: Guilty, I would not.
sentences.zh: 惭愧，我确实不会。

sentences.en: So, Alex, I want you to talk through the story, the visual story that this tapestry actually
sentences.zh: 那么，亚历克斯，我想请你讲讲这个故事，这幅挂毯实际上描绘的视觉故事，

sentences.en: depicts because I think that will help our American brains to grasp why this embroidery, as you say, has become one of the hottest tickets in London right now.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为这有助于我们美国人的大脑理解为什么这件刺绣，正如你所说，成为了伦敦目前最热门的入场券之一。

sentences.en: So the Sparknakes version, the start of the tapestry, Edward the Confessor, King of England.
sentences.zh: 故事的开端，也就是挂毯的开头，是英格兰国王“忏悔者”爱德华。

sentences.en: He's childless, he's ill, he knows he needs an heir.
sentences.zh: 他没有子嗣，身体抱恙，他知道自己需要一个继承人。

sentences.en: So he talks to Harold Godwinson, his brother-in-law, and sends him off to France to the Norman
sentences.zh: 于是他与妹夫哈罗德·戈德温森商量，派他去法国找诺曼底公爵威廉。

sentences.en: King, Duke William.
sentences.zh: 威廉公爵。

sentences.en: Harold meets William, basically says, you can come and be King of England when Edward dies.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德见到威廉，基本上是说，爱德华死后你可以来当英格兰国王。

sentences.en: My brother has no heirs, we nominate you.
sentences.zh: 我哥哥没有继承人，我们提名你。

sentences.en: Come over, turn England into your kingdom.
sentences.zh: 过来吧，把英格兰变成你的王国。

sentences.en: You seem a great guy.
sentences.zh: 你看起来是个不错的人。

sentences.en: Harold in the tapestry has quite a devilish mustache, and he looks a bit like someone you might have seen in 1970s porn film in America.
sentences.zh: 挂毯上的哈罗德留着相当邪恶的胡子，看起来有点像你在美国70年代色情电影里看到的人。

sentences.en: I've seen Boogie Nights, he looks like he's walked out of one of those sets.
sentences.zh: 我看过《不羁夜》，他看起来就像是从那些片场走出来的一样。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, did you say Boogie Nights?
sentences.zh: 抱歉，你刚才说《不羁夜》？

sentences.en: Boogie Nights, isn't that the film?
sentences.zh: 《不羁夜》，那不是那部电影吗？

sentences.en: No, yeah, absolutely, they boogie all night.
sentences.zh: 不，是的，绝对是，他们整晚都在“不羁”。

sentences.en: So he just looks very, very loose, and that might give a hint about what's to come.
sentences.zh: 所以他看起来非常、非常放荡，这可能暗示了接下来要发生的事情。

sentences.en: Back in England, Edward dies, and Harold decides to pull a fast one, essentially.
sentences.zh: 回到英格兰，爱德华去世了，哈罗德决定耍个花招，本质上是这样。

sentences.en: He is soon on the throne himself.
sentences.zh: 他很快就自己登上了王位。

sentences.en: Oh, so he reneges, he pulls a Dick Cheney, he says, I will be your actual leader, forget the promises I've made to William over there in France.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以他背信弃义，他玩了一手“迪克·切尼”，他说，我才是你们真正的领袖，忘了我对法国那边威廉许下的承诺吧。

sentences.en: Assuming he actually did that, it is a tapestry of the victors, is their story.
sentences.zh: 假设他真的这么做了，这毕竟是胜利者的挂毯，是他们的故事。

sentences.en: So the tapestry does not depict him twirling his mustache evilly, but you could imagine him at that moment doing just that.
sentences.zh: 所以挂毯并没有描绘他邪恶地捻着胡子，但你可以想象他在那一刻确实就是这么做的。

sentences.en: Word obviously gets to William in France.
sentences.zh: 消息显然传到了法国的威廉耳中。

sentences.en: How could it not?
sentences.zh: 怎么可能传不到呢？

sentences.en: And William is pissed.
sentences.zh: 威廉气疯了。

sentences.en: He is like, what on earth has that guy done?
sentences.zh: 他心想，那家伙到底干了什么？

sentences.en: He doesn't wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 他一刻也没耽误。

sentences.en: He sends all his men off to build a fleet.
sentences.zh: 他派所有人去建造舰队。

sentences.en: He is going to invade.
sentences.zh: 他要入侵。

sentences.en: He's going to take that throne for himself.
sentences.zh: 他要为自己夺回王位。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And we are now in 1066, this pivotal year in English history, the year every child learns in school.
sentences.zh: 我们现在来到了1066年，这是英国历史上关键的一年，每个孩子在学校里都会学到这一年。

sentences.en: Like, people even say, like, 1066 and all that.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至会说，比如“1066年及其他”之类的。

sentences.en: You don't even have to know what it means.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不需要知道它意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so very soon, William is landing in England with his forces on the south coast, and he is causing havoc.
sentences.zh: 很快，威廉带着他的军队在英格兰南海岸登陆，开始制造混乱。

sentences.en: You know, he starts burning down villages.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他开始烧毁村庄。

sentences.en: It's the perennial raping and pillaging that we all know from history.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们从历史中熟知的永恒的掠夺和杀戮。

sentences.en: When I was actually in the British Museum looking at this recently, there were some children
sentences.zh: 最近我在大英博物馆看这个的时候，有一些孩子，

sentences.en: who their teacher was trying to tell them about this era and say, like, what did I tell you
sentences.zh: 他们的老师正试图给他们讲那个时代，说，我告诉过你们

sentences.en: William was doing in Britain?
sentences.zh: 威廉在英国做了什么吗？

sentences.en: And the children replied that he was rage-baiting.
sentences.zh: 孩子们回答说他在“激怒诱饵”。

sentences.en: He was rage-baiting Harold.
sentences.zh: 他在用激将法对付哈罗德。

sentences.en: So yeah, William rage-baits his way through southern England, and eventually Harold decides he has to confront him.
sentences.zh: 没错，威廉一路激将，横扫英格兰南部，最终哈罗德决定必须与他正面对抗。

sentences.en: And there is this huge battle.
sentences.zh: 于是爆发了一场大战。

sentences.en: There is carnage.
sentences.zh: 到处都是杀戮。

sentences.en: The battle goes on all day.
sentences.zh: 战斗持续了一整天。

sentences.en: Most medieval battles apparently only lasted a few hours.
sentences.zh: 据说大多数中世纪的战斗只持续几个小时。

sentences.en: This goes on.
sentences.zh: 这场战斗却一直持续。

sentences.en: It is bloody.
sentences.zh: 非常血腥。

sentences.en: According to the tapestry, there are beheadings.
sentences.zh: 根据挂毯记载，有斩首的场面。

sentences.en: There's bones going everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是尸骨。

sentences.en: And eventually, William succeeds.
sentences.zh: 最终，威廉获胜了。

sentences.en: Harold, isolated, is, history says, shot in the head by an arrow.
sentences.zh: 历史记载，孤立无援的哈罗德被箭射中头部而死。

sentences.en: That leaves the English throne free for William.
sentences.zh: 这让英格兰王位空了出来，留给了威廉。

sentences.en: He becomes William the Conqueror, and he takes over England, changing the course of the country's history.
sentences.zh: 他成为了“征服者威廉”，接管了英格兰，改变了国家历史的进程。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That is quite a drama.
sentences.zh: 这真是太戏剧性了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, so far, what you're describing, and what this tapestry enshrines, sounds a whole lot like British defeat, and a pretty humiliating defeat, I might add.
sentences.zh: 所以，到目前为止，你所描述的以及这幅挂毯所铭记的，听起来很像是英国的战败，而且我得说，是一场相当羞辱性的战败。

sentences.en: Political, military, cultural over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，在政治、军事和文化上都是如此。

sentences.en: And so, I guess I'm struggling to see...
sentences.zh: 所以我很难理解……

sentences.en: Why would this celebrate?
sentences.zh: 为什么这值得庆祝？

sentences.en: Why would this become a beloved artifact, and so central to British identity?
sentences.zh: 为什么它会成为一件深受喜爱的文物，并成为英国身份认同的核心？

sentences.en: It might be a humiliating defeat, but it is also, it's an event that completely changed
sentences.zh: 这可能是一场羞辱性的战败，但它也是一个彻底改变了

sentences.en: English culture.
sentences.zh: 英国文化的事件。

sentences.en: You know, it changed our language.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它改变了我们的语言。

sentences.en: It changed our laws.
sentences.zh: 它改变了我们的法律。

sentences.en: It changed the aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 它改变了贵族阶层。

sentences.en: And so, for that, it is key to Britain's history.
sentences.zh: 因此，它对英国历史至关重要。

sentences.en: And also, it's so foundational, perhaps because we have this tapestry.
sentences.zh: 而且，它如此基础，或许是因为我们拥有这幅挂毯。

sentences.en: If we didn't have this, you know, this artwork that documents it in the most accessible, simplistic, and at times even funny, as well as brutal way.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有这件艺术品，你知道的，这件以最平易近人、最简单，有时甚至是有趣且残酷的方式记录历史的作品。

sentences.en: If we didn't have this one-off, unique artifact, maybe we wouldn't remember it as much.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有这件独一无二的文物，也许我们对它的记忆就不会那么深刻了。

sentences.en: It's just become part of the fabric here.
sentences.zh: 它已经成为了这里文化结构的一部分。

sentences.en: So to speak.
sentences.zh: 可以这么说。

sentences.en: So to speak, yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以这么说，没错。

sentences.en: So in the aftermath of this pretty major British defeat and humiliation, who commissions the creation of this tapestry to tell the story of Britain going to pieces here?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这次重大的英国战败和羞辱之后，是谁委托创作了这幅挂毯，来讲述英国在这里分崩离析的故事呢？

sentences.en: There's one slight problem with the Bayou Tapestry, which is there's a lot is unknown.
sentences.zh: 巴约挂毯有一个小问题，那就是有很多未知之处。

sentences.en: But historians think it was commissioned by a guy called Bishop Odo, who was William the
sentences.zh: 但历史学家认为，它是受一位名叫奥多主教的人委托创作的，他是威廉征服者的同父异母兄弟。

sentences.en: Conqueror's half-brother.
sentences.zh: 征服者的同父异母兄弟。

sentences.en: The reason they think he commissioned it is because he was probably not a very big figure in all these events of 1066, but he appears throughout the tapestry, even in the climactic
sentences.zh: 他们认为是他委托创作的原因是，他在1066年的所有这些事件中可能并不是一个大人物，但他却贯穿了整幅挂毯，甚至出现在了高潮的

sentences.en: battle scenes.
sentences.zh: 战斗场景中。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: He likely commissioned it in Canterbury in England, which had the best embroiderers at the time.
sentences.zh: 他很可能是在英国的坎特伯雷委托制作的，那里当时拥有最好的绣工。

sentences.en: And they made it probably for the renovated cathedral in Bayou.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能是为巴约翻新后的教堂制作的。

sentences.en: So as soon as they finished making it, it was probably spirited across the English Channel to France.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦制作完成，它很可能就被迅速运过了英吉利海峡，送到了法国。

sentences.en: And it's been there ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后它就一直留在那里。

sentences.en: Why does it never, ever somehow return to Britain from France?
sentences.zh: 为什么它从来、从来没有从法国回到过英国？

sentences.en: These two countries are geographically close and over time develop fairly warm relations.
sentences.zh: 这两个国家地理位置相近，随着时间的推移，关系也相当融洽。

sentences.en: So how come it remains essentially walled off from Britain?
sentences.zh: 那么它怎么会一直与英国隔绝呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's not for a lack of trying.
sentences.zh: 嗯，并不是因为没有尝试过。

sentences.en: I mean, Britain's wanted this item on loan for decades.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，英国几十年来一直想借用这件物品。

sentences.en: But in France, they just say this is too fragile to ever send abroad.
sentences.zh: 但在法国，他们只会说这太脆弱了，不能送到国外。

sentences.en: And that's a good reason, because throughout its history, the tapestry has been manhandled.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的理由，因为在它的整个历史中，这幅挂毯一直被粗暴对待。

sentences.en: It's been transported along bumpy roads.
sentences.zh: 它曾被运送在颠簸的道路上。

sentences.en: I mean, at one point, Napoleon brought it to Paris and displayed it in the Louvre, because
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一次，拿破仑把它带到了巴黎，并在卢浮宫展出，因为

sentences.en: he saw it as a sort of a good way of showing, maybe I've got links to William the Conqueror.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是一种很好的方式来展示，也许我和威廉征服者有联系。

sentences.en: I can take over Britain too.
sentences.zh: 我也能接管英国。

sentences.en: At one point, the Nazis started moving it around.
sentences.zh: 有一次，纳粹开始四处转移它。

sentences.en: They saw it as both a emblematic example of German culture, but also they saw it as foreshadowing their own desire to take over England.
sentences.zh: 他们既将其视为德国文化的象征，也将其视为他们自己想要接管英国的预兆。

sentences.en: Wow, so when the Nazis occupied France, they're moving it around, but they managed, I suppose, because of its scale, not to take it out of France.
sentences.zh: 哇，所以当纳粹占领法国时，他们在四处转移它，但我猜是因为它的规模，他们没能把它带出法国。

sentences.en: They tried desperately to take it out of France.
sentences.zh: 他们拼命想把它带出法国。

sentences.en: Towards the end, they wanted to get it to Berlin, but the Allied invasion fortunately got to
sentences.zh: 在最后关头，他们想把它运到柏林，但幸运的是，盟军在他们设法把它运走之前就到达了

sentences.en: Paris just before they managed to get it out.
sentences.zh: 巴黎。

sentences.en: They have infamously left a cigar burn on it.
sentences.zh: 他们臭名昭著地在上面留下了一个雪茄烧痕。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: When we get to sort of post-World War II, this thing has folds in it, tears in it, stains in it, rips.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入二战后时期，这东西上面有褶皱、撕裂、污渍和破损。

sentences.en: I mean, it is an incredibly delicate document.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是一份极其脆弱的文件。

sentences.en: So as soon as the British start really seriously saying, can we have it, you know, especially for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation, they say, can we bring it to London?
sentences.zh: 所以当英国人开始真正认真地提出，我们能借用它吗，你知道，特别是为了伊丽莎白二世女王的加冕典礼，他们说，我们能把它带到伦敦吗？

sentences.en: They start saying, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 他们开始说，不，不，不。

sentences.en: We're not moving this under any circumstance.
sentences.zh: 无论如何我们都不会移动它。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I'm hearing that French voice in my head.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里听到了那个法国口音。

sentences.en: No, no, no, monsieur, it is not possible.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，先生，这不可能。

sentences.en: It is not possible.
sentences.zh: 这不可能。

sentences.en: I think you're exactly right.
sentences.zh: 我想你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: Well, then the inevitable question is, what changed and what happened that suddenly made
sentences.zh: 那么不可避免的问题是，发生了什么变化，是什么让这件200多英尺长的文物的脆弱性

sentences.en: the fragility of this 200-and-something-foot-long artifact no longer an obstacle to moving it from France to Britain?
sentences.zh: 不再成为将其从法国运往英国的障碍？

sentences.en: It all comes down to one man, Emmanuel Macron.
sentences.zh: 这一切都归结于一个人，埃马纽埃尔·马克龙。

sentences.en: He is the egotist behind this impossible loan.
sentences.zh: 他就是这次不可能的借展背后的自负者。

sentences.en: The impossible loan.
sentences.zh: 不可能的借展。

sentences.en: Well, we're going to talk about the impossible loan and how it comes to be right after the break.
sentences.zh: 好吧，休息之后，我们将讨论这次不可能的借展以及它是如何实现的。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: Alex, tell us the story of this impossible loan overseen by the president of France that somehow brings this tapestry embroidery to London.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，给我们讲讲这个由法国总统监督的、不知何故将这幅挂毯刺绣带到伦敦的“不可能的借展”的故事。

sentences.en: So this actually, like everything in the tapestry, is an annoyingly long story.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上，就像挂毯里的一切一样，是一个令人烦恼的长故事。

sentences.en: It starts in 2018, when there's an Anglo-French summit for re-establishing our friendship post-Brexit.
sentences.zh: 它始于2018年，当时举行了一次英法峰会，旨在重建我们脱欧后的友谊。

sentences.en: You know, Britain's left the European Union.
sentences.zh: 你知道，英国离开了欧盟。

sentences.en: Relations are really bad.
sentences.zh: 关系真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: Macron decides, I know how I can repair things.
sentences.zh: 马克龙决定，我知道我该如何修复关系。

sentences.en: I'll announce I'm going to loan the tapestry.
sentences.zh: 我宣布我要借出这幅挂毯。

sentences.en: And the reaction in France is one, at least in the conservation world, one of horror.
sentences.zh: 而在法国，至少在文物保护界，反应是一片惊恐。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not happening.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不可能发生。

sentences.en: You are not loaning this item.
sentences.zh: 你不能借出这件物品。

sentences.en: I mean, I've spoken to a former head of the Bay of Tapestry Museum who said when she heard about it, she just thought he was, you know, taking the piss.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我采访过一位巴约挂毯博物馆的前馆长，她说当她听到这个消息时，她只是觉得他在，你知道，胡闹。

sentences.en: She thought it was insane.
sentences.zh: 她觉得这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Like, this is never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 就像，这永远不会发生。

sentences.en: And it looked like she was right.
sentences.zh: 看起来她是正确的。

sentences.en: Because it just, it quickly disappears off the agenda.
sentences.zh: 因为它很快就从议程上消失了。

sentences.en: There was such strong opposition to this.
sentences.zh: 对此有如此强烈的反对意见。

sentences.en: I mean, even in Britain, the artist David Hockney, before he died, he at one point wrote an opinion
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使在英国，艺术家大卫·霍克尼在去世前也曾写过一篇评论文章

sentences.en: piece saying, as an artist, I am reckless, but I would never do something as reckless as this.
sentences.zh: 说，作为一名艺术家，我很鲁莽，但我永远不会做这么鲁莽的事情。

sentences.en: So everyone is remembering the carelessness of the Nazis and Napoleon and thinking to
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都在回忆纳粹和拿破仑的粗心大意，并心想

sentences.en: themselves, even under the best of circumstances, with professional movers and preservationists involved, this is going to go horribly sideways.
sentences.zh: 即使在最好的情况下，有专业的搬运工和文物保护人员参与，这也可能会变得极其糟糕。

sentences.en: I think even people who didn't remember Napoleon or the Nazis were thinking this could go sideways.
sentences.zh: 我想即使是那些不记得拿破仑或纳粹的人也认为这可能会出问题。

sentences.en: You just don't, you know, you don't take risks with artifacts of such world renown.
sentences.zh: 你只是不能，你知道，你不能拿如此举世闻名的文物去冒险。

sentences.en: You know, it'd be like, you know, the Louvre does not want to move the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像，卢浮宫不想移动《蒙娜丽莎》一样。

sentences.en: You know, the Italians don't want to stick Michelangelo's David in a crate and put it on tour around
sentences.zh: 你知道，意大利人不想把米开朗基罗的《大卫》装进板条箱，然后带它去

sentences.en: America.
sentences.zh: 美国巡回展出。

sentences.en: You just don't risk a world masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 你只是不能拿世界杰作去冒险。

sentences.en: And then suddenly...
sentences.zh: 然后突然间……

sentences.en: We did our best not to be put in the situation to make this loan of biotech.
sentences.zh: 我们尽了最大努力不让自己陷入借出巴约挂毯的境地。

sentences.en: Last year, Macron is back again.
sentences.zh: 去年，马克龙又回来了。

sentences.en: And we found the best experts of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了世界上最好的专家。

sentences.en: And he's at the British Museum.
sentences.zh: 他在大英博物馆。

sentences.en: To explain in perfect details why it was totally impossible.
sentences.zh: 详细解释了为什么这完全不可能。

sentences.en: And he says...
sentences.zh: 他说……

sentences.en: We went beyond the experts.
sentences.zh: 我们超越了专家。

sentences.en: This loan is happening.
sentences.zh: 这次借展正在进行。

sentences.en: We have gone beyond the experts.
sentences.zh: 我们已经超越了专家。

sentences.en: And we managed to find great solutions.
sentences.zh: 我们设法找到了很好的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's almost saying we have been reckless.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是在说我们一直很鲁莽。

sentences.en: So merci, mesdames les ministres.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢各位部长女士。

sentences.en: But for political, diplomatic, showmanship reasons, we are making this happen.
sentences.zh: 但出于政治、外交和作秀的原因，我们正在促成这件事。

sentences.en: OK, so once CanDo Macron decides that France can do this, what are the logistics involved in actually making this loan happen?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么一旦“能做先生”马克龙决定法国可以做到这一点，实现这次借展涉及哪些后勤工作？

sentences.en: I think there are actually two key reasons why this happens.
sentences.zh: 我认为这发生的原因实际上有两个关键点。

sentences.en: One, the museum in Bayer is closing for renovation.
sentences.zh: 第一，巴约的博物馆正在关闭进行翻新。

sentences.en: So you have an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 所以你有一个机会。

sentences.en: This is going to have to go off display anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，它都必须撤展。

sentences.en: So if you are putting it into a box, why not put it into a box and then transport that box across the English Channel?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你要把它装进盒子里，为什么不把它装进盒子里，然后把那个盒子运过英吉利海峡呢？

sentences.en: Well, the other thing is France and Britain so wanted this to happen that they were willing to pay for the science and the conservation techniques to make this work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，另一件事是法国和英国非常希望这件事发生，以至于他们愿意为实现这一目标的科学和保护技术买单。

sentences.en: I mean, I spoke to a conservator recently who said, you know, what they would normally do for moving a tapestry like this is put it on the floor, put a roller on top of it
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我最近采访了一位文物保护员，他说，你知道，他们通常移动这样的挂毯的做法是把它放在地板上，在上面放一个滚筒

sentences.en: and roll it up.
sentences.zh: 然后把它卷起来。

sentences.en: And that is the most dangerous thing, you know, for such a delicate artifact, that would be foolhardy.
sentences.zh: 这是最危险的事情，你知道，对于这样一件精致的文物，那将是愚蠢的。

sentences.en: But what they've done for this is like Star Trek.
sentences.zh: 但他们为此所做的事情就像《星际迷航》一样。

sentences.en: You know, so much money and technology has been put into this one move.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这次搬运投入了太多的金钱和技术。

sentences.en: It's like nothing these conservators have seen before.
sentences.zh: 这就像这些文物保护员以前从未见过的一样。

sentences.en: OK, well, describe some of the Star Trek-worthy steps that have been taken to make this seamless.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么描述一下为使这次搬运天衣无缝而采取的一些《星际迷航》级别的步骤。

sentences.en: It is really delicate, precise work.
sentences.zh: 这是非常精细、精确的工作。

sentences.en: Initially in Bayer, the tapestry was hanging by curtain hooks to a curtain rail.
sentences.zh: 最初在巴约，挂毯是用窗帘钩挂在窗帘轨道上的。

sentences.en: They had to work out how to get it off that safely into a crate.
sentences.zh: 他们必须想出如何安全地把它从上面取下来装进板条箱。

sentences.en: What they ended up coming up with after lots of scientists put lots of studies is they got a hundred people to stand along the length of it and move it like two inches at a time.
sentences.zh: 在许多科学家进行了大量研究后，他们最终想出的办法是找了一百个人沿着它的长度站立，一次移动两英寸。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: There's these amazing videos of a woman with a headset.
sentences.zh: 有一些令人惊叹的视频，显示一个戴着耳机的女人。

sentences.en: It's almost a military operation.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是一次军事行动。

sentences.en: You can almost see the beads of sweat dripping off their faces with nervous energy as they try and move it without risking damaging it.
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以看到他们脸上因为紧张而流下的汗珠，因为他们试图在不冒损坏风险的情况下移动它。

sentences.en: Once they get it off this curtain rail, they put it onto, and I'm sorry this is sounding so dense, but they put it onto another rail, which then folds up.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们把它从窗帘轨道上取下来，他们就把它放在，我很抱歉这听起来很复杂，但他们把它放在了另一条轨道上，然后折叠起来。

sentences.en: So you end up with a tapestry in almost like a concertina shape, very loose, which is then put into a box.
sentences.zh: 所以你最终得到的是一个几乎呈手风琴形状的挂毯，非常松散，然后被放入一个盒子里。

sentences.en: Normally, if you are transporting a work of art across the ocean, you just put that into a wooden crate, drive it there.
sentences.zh: 通常，如果你要跨洋运输一件艺术品，你只需把它放进一个木箱里，开车运过去。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What they do is put that crate into another crate.
sentences.zh: 他们做的是把那个板条箱放进另一个板条箱里。

sentences.en: I mean, bear with me, which is surrounded by springs that are basically used in earthquake zones.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，请耐心听我说，它被基本上用于地震区的弹簧所包围。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the people who worked on it described it as like, you know, an old school baby carriage.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中一位参与这项工作的人将其描述为，你知道，老式的婴儿车。

sentences.en: You know, you should be able to take this tapestry along a bouncy road and it will not wake up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你应该能够带着这幅挂毯走在颠簸的路上，它也不会醒来。

sentences.en: It is not going to start crying and screaming at you.
sentences.zh: 它不会开始对你哭闹。

sentences.en: But then even once they'd come up with this, you know, technology used to stop buildings falling down.
sentences.zh: 但即使在他们想出这个之后，你知道，用于防止建筑物倒塌的技术。

sentences.en: That isn't the end.
sentences.zh: 那还不是终点。

sentences.en: They then come up with the routes to take it to London.
sentences.zh: 他们随后制定了前往伦敦的路线。

sentences.en: They drive that route several times to work out where the potholes are.
sentences.zh: 他们多次驾驶那条路线，以找出坑洼在哪里。

sentences.en: Good Lord.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So they can then analyze this even more to make sure it is safe as possible.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以进一步分析，以确保它尽可能安全。

sentences.en: Once all that is done, every measure is taken to make it safe, they are then still worried
sentences.zh: 一旦所有这些都完成了，采取了每一项措施来确保它的安全，他们仍然担心

sentences.en: that when they drive this, maybe some terrorist, maybe an eco-protester is going to try and steal this.
sentences.zh: 当他们开车运送它时，也许会有恐怖分子，也许会有生态抗议者试图偷走它。

sentences.en: Naturally.
sentences.zh: 很自然。

sentences.en: So you do all this work and then you get to July the 9th this year.
sentences.zh: 所以你做了所有这些工作，然后到了今年的7月9日。

sentences.en: It's 6.15pm.
sentences.zh: 下午6点15分。

sentences.en: A bright yellow truck leaves Bayer.
sentences.zh: 一辆亮黄色的卡车离开了巴约。

sentences.en: The tapestry is in the back.
sentences.zh: 挂毯就在后面。

sentences.en: They get the French security service to accompany it in the highest secretive midnight move.
sentences.zh: 他们让法国安全部门在最高机密的午夜行动中护送它。

sentences.en: That truck drives onto a train.
sentences.zh: 那辆卡车开上了一列火车。

sentences.en: The train goes to Britain.
sentences.zh: 火车开往英国。

sentences.en: The truck drives off it and then goes incredibly slowly through the night to the British Museum.
sentences.zh: 卡车开下车，然后在夜色中以极慢的速度驶向大英博物馆。

sentences.en: But then, of course, it has to be unpacked.
sentences.zh: 但当然，之后还得进行拆箱。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, yes.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，确实如此。

sentences.en: The operation to get it out of that crate was just as rigorous and involved as the one to get it out of the display in Bayer.
sentences.zh: 将它从板条箱中取出的过程，和当初从拜厄的展柜中取出的过程一样严谨且复杂。

sentences.en: There, again, about 100 people lined up.
sentences.zh: 在那里，同样有大约100人排队等候。

sentences.en: They opened the crate on this folding panel so delicately.
sentences.zh: 他们非常小心地在折叠板上打开了板条箱。

sentences.en: They checked every single panel to make sure the tapestry, once unfolded, wasn't ripped, wasn't damaged.
sentences.zh: 他们检查了每一块嵌板，以确保挂毯在展开后没有撕裂或损坏。

sentences.en: They then had to lift it very delicately onto a railing that then went up to the ceiling
sentences.zh: 然后，他们必须非常小心地将其抬到栏杆上，再升至天花板，

sentences.en: of this exhibition hall in the British Museum and then lowered the tapestry onto a specially designed table, which cost £2 million.
sentences.zh: 也就是大英博物馆这个展厅的天花板，随后将挂毯降到一张特制的桌子上，那张桌子花了200万英镑。

sentences.en: One table?
sentences.zh: 就一张桌子？

sentences.en: I should actually Google that.
sentences.zh: 我其实应该去谷歌查一下。

sentences.en: Two GBP, two USD.
sentences.zh: 两英镑，两美元。

sentences.en: God, $2.7 million.
sentences.zh: 天哪，270万美元。

sentences.en: Is it made out of gold?
sentences.zh: 它是金子做的吗？

sentences.en: Looks like it's made out of wood, actually.
sentences.zh: 看起来其实像是木头做的。

sentences.en: It's got very thick glass.
sentences.zh: 它有很厚的玻璃罩。

sentences.en: It's temperature controlled.
sentences.zh: 而且是恒温控制的。

sentences.en: You know, it's basically the greatest table you could ever have if you wanted to display a unique tapestry in one long 220-feet line.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你想把一幅独特的挂毯以一条220英尺长的直线展示出来，这基本上是你所能拥有的最棒的桌子了。

sentences.en: I mean, it only just squeezes into the British Museum.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它刚好能塞进大英博物馆。

sentences.en: I think there's something like 20 centimeters clearance.
sentences.zh: 我想大约只有20厘米的间隙。

sentences.en: That is snug.
sentences.zh: 那真是严丝合缝。

sentences.en: The British Museum were telling me that they'd written to Guinness, hoping to get the Guinness world record for the longest ever art table.
sentences.zh: 大英博物馆的人告诉我，他们已经写信给吉尼斯，希望能获得最长艺术展示桌的吉尼斯世界纪录。

sentences.en: Sounds a bit niche.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点小众。

sentences.en: I did tell them that was a bit desperate.
sentences.zh: 我确实告诉他们，这显得有点绝望。

sentences.en: But, you know, all publicity is good publicity, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我想任何宣传都是好的宣传。

sentences.en: So once all of this painstaking, cumbersome moving by truck and crate and hundreds of hands is done, what condition is the tapestry in when it arrives?
sentences.zh: 那么，在经历了所有这些通过卡车、板条箱和数百人之手进行的繁琐搬运工作后，挂毯到达时处于什么状态？

sentences.en: Is this a success?
sentences.zh: 这是一次成功吗？

sentences.en: Yes, apparently so.
sentences.zh: 是的，显然如此。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone I've spoken to in very relieved tones says it is perfectly fine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我采访过的每个人都以非常如释重负的语气说它完好无损。

sentences.en: They found two threads that have broken, but that is two among millions.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了两根断裂的线，但这可是数百万根线中的两根。

sentences.en: They also found some fibers in the bottom of the crate, but those might not be from the tapestry.
sentences.zh: 他们还在板条箱底部发现了一些纤维，但那些可能不是来自挂毯。

sentences.en: They might be from, like, the jumper of one of the hundreds of people who was involved in moving this.
sentences.zh: 它们可能来自参与搬运的数百人中某人的毛衣。

sentences.en: I mean, when I actually learned of these breakages, I went to the main objector in France, a guy called Didier Reichner, who runs an art magazine, and I sort of told him about this
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我得知这些破损时，我去找了法国的主要反对者，一个叫迪迪埃·赖希纳的人，他经营着一本艺术杂志，我把这件事告诉了他，

sentences.en: in almost expecting him to be up in arMs.
sentences.zh: 几乎预料到他会大发雷霆。

sentences.en: You were baiting him.
sentences.zh: 你在诱导他。

sentences.en: I'm a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 我是个记者。

sentences.en: I was obviously impartial.
sentences.zh: 我显然是公正的。

sentences.en: I did not mind what response he gave me.
sentences.zh: 我不介意他给我什么回应。

sentences.en: But he seems mildly nonplussed by it all.
sentences.zh: 但他对这一切似乎感到有些困惑。

sentences.en: It's a triumph.
sentences.zh: 这是一个胜利。

sentences.en: It is a triumph.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个胜利。

sentences.en: So when it opened just over a week ago, I made sure I was one of the first through the door.
sentences.zh: 所以当它在一周多前开放时，我确保自己是第一批进门的人之一。

sentences.en: And to my completely untrained eyes, it looked perfectly fine.
sentences.zh: 在我这个完全外行的人看来，它看起来非常完美。

sentences.en: Okay, well, let's talk about what it was like for you to actually see this in the museum on its very fancy table right after the break.
sentences.zh: 好的，休息之后，我们来谈谈你在博物馆里亲眼看到那张非常昂贵的桌子上的挂毯是什么感觉。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Okay, Alex, set the scene for us.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚历克斯，为我们描述一下现场。

sentences.en: It is tapestry day for you there in London.
sentences.zh: 对你来说，伦敦今天是挂毯日。

sentences.en: How does it unfold?
sentences.zh: 它是如何展开的？

sentences.en: I turned up outside the British Museum in central London for 10am to be one of the first people through those gates.
sentences.zh: 我早上10点出现在伦敦市中心的大英博物馆外，想成为第一批穿过大门的人之一。

sentences.en: And there's already a queue of people.
sentences.zh: 那里已经排起了长队。

sentences.en: We all shuffled into this line and walk into this huge, long, dark room.
sentences.zh: 我们都挪动着进入这条队伍，走进这个巨大、狭长且昏暗的房间。

sentences.en: And there it is.
sentences.zh: 它就在那里。

sentences.en: And we walked along its length.
sentences.zh: 我们沿着它的长度走着。

sentences.en: I'm looking at literally the first scene.
sentences.zh: 我看到的正是第一幕。

sentences.en: The staff trying to tell us to quicken up.
sentences.zh: 工作人员试图催促我们快点走。

sentences.en: I'm now in front of scene 17 and showing some of the Norman soldiers getting caught in quicksand.
sentences.zh: 我现在站在第17幕前，上面展示了一些诺曼士兵陷入流沙的情景。

sentences.en: And it's just amazing how much these embroiderers managed to pack into this thing.
sentences.zh: 这些刺绣者能在这件作品中塞进这么多内容，真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: A comet has appeared.
sentences.zh: 一颗彗星出现了。

sentences.en: It's Hayley's Comet.
sentences.zh: 那是哈雷彗星。

sentences.en: You can tell it's a bad omen because people are looking at this comet and pointing up at it with horror.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出这是一个坏兆头，因为人们正看着这颗彗星，惊恐地指着它。

sentences.en: I am now surrounded by school kids and hoping they move along.
sentences.zh: 我现在被一群小学生包围了，希望他们能快点走。

sentences.en: The children in my visit just kept stopping at certain scenes.
sentences.zh: 我参观时，孩子们总是停在某些场景前。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: The more gruesome ones.
sentences.zh: 那些更恐怖的场景。

sentences.en: There's a lot of nudity.
sentences.zh: 有很多裸体画面。

sentences.en: The risque ones.
sentences.zh: 那些大胆的场景。

sentences.en: Looks like he's pleading with her to let them be together.
sentences.zh: 看起来他是在恳求她让他们在一起。

sentences.en: And she's sort of going, oh, not again.
sentences.zh: 而她似乎在说，哦，别再这样了。

sentences.en: And there are 58 scenes.
sentences.zh: 一共有58个场景。

sentences.en: The tapestry shows this man holding an arrow in his eye.
sentences.zh: 挂毯上画着一个男人，眼睛里插着一支箭。

sentences.en: And Harold Godwinson is dead.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·戈德温森死了。

sentences.en: That is the end.
sentences.zh: 这就是结局。

sentences.en: William the Conqueror has conquered England.
sentences.zh: 征服者威廉征服了英格兰。

sentences.en: But as you're going along, for me what hit me was almost the connection to the people of Must Woven This, who sewed it.
sentences.zh: 但当你走过时，对我来说，最触动我的是与那些编织它、缝制它的人们的联系。

sentences.en: Because the images, they look like a cartoon that could have been made, you know, like three years ago.
sentences.zh: 因为这些图像看起来就像一部卡通片，你知道，就像三年前制作的一样。

sentences.en: It looks like something out of a Japanese anime studio.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像是日本动画工作室的作品。

sentences.en: All the characters have, like Harold Godwinson, as I said, like he has this very loose mustache.
sentences.zh: 所有的角色，就像我说的哈罗德·戈德温森，他留着这种非常随意的胡子。

sentences.en: His, like, eyebrows, you can see them.
sentences.zh: 他的眉毛，你可以看得很清楚。

sentences.en: They're almost sort of done in quizzical expressions.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎呈现出一种疑惑的表情。

sentences.en: You know, there are all these sort of quirky elements to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，里面有各种各样古怪的元素。

sentences.en: There are bits that look like surrealist painting.
sentences.zh: 有些部分看起来像超现实主义绘画。

sentences.en: And I, as a British person, there are many things that obviously I dislike about my country.
sentences.zh: 作为一个英国人，我显然不喜欢我国家的很多事情。

sentences.en: You know, there are things I regret.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些事情我感到后悔。

sentences.en: We are an empire.
sentences.zh: 我们曾经是一个帝国。

sentences.en: We just, you know, we colonized half the world.
sentences.zh: 我们，你知道，殖民了半个世界。

sentences.en: We did lots of brutal, horrific things.
sentences.zh: 我们做了很多残忍、可怕的事情。

sentences.en: But one thing I do really like is our sense of creativity, our humor, and our absurdity.
sentences.zh: 但我确实非常喜欢的一点是我们的创造力、幽默感和荒诞感。

sentences.en: And all of that is in this tapestry.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都体现在这幅挂毯中。

sentences.en: There are in-jokes.
sentences.zh: 里面有内部笑话。

sentences.en: There's nudity.
sentences.zh: 有裸体画面。

sentences.en: There are 93 penises in this thing.
sentences.zh: 这东西里有93个阴茎。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, 93 penises, you say?
sentences.zh: 抱歉，抱歉，你说有93个阴茎？

sentences.en: There's an academic debate about one of them.
sentences.zh: 关于其中一个，学术界还有争论。

sentences.en: 88 of them belong to horses, but the rest are human.
sentences.zh: 其中88个属于马，其余的是人的。

sentences.en: You know, there are things you wouldn't expect.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些事情是你意想不到的。

sentences.en: For example, 93 penises.
sentences.zh: 例如，93个阴茎。

sentences.en: I'm really getting from you just how epic this tapestry is.
sentences.zh: 我真的从你那里感受到了这幅挂毯是多么史诗般宏大。

sentences.en: And I want to ask you, now that you have seen it and you've spent all this time with it, if there's one scene, one moment in particular, that struck you most deeply.
sentences.zh: 我想问你，既然你已经看过它，并且花了很多时间陪伴它，有没有哪一个场景或瞬间最深刻地触动了你？

sentences.en: The one I know I'm going to remember, I doubt anyone else would ever say this, but it is men suddenly chopping down trees to make the boats to invade England.
sentences.zh: 我知道我会记住的那一个，我怀疑别人会不会这么说，但那是男人们突然砍伐树木来制造船只以入侵英格兰的场景。

sentences.en: And it didn't hit me emotionally.
sentences.zh: 它并没有在情感上击中我。

sentences.en: Your face looks very quizzical, Michael, like you're saying,
sentences.zh: 你的表情看起来很疑惑，迈克尔，好像在说，

sentences.en: God, why pick something more exciting?
sentences.zh: 天哪，为什么不选个更刺激的？

sentences.en: But the figures just had such movement to them.
sentences.zh: 但这些人物的动作感太强了。

sentences.en: These were ordinary people, like swinging axes, trying to build boats.
sentences.zh: 这些是普通人，像是在挥舞斧头，试图建造船只。

sentences.en: And like suddenly I thought, oh, right, this is art.
sentences.zh: 突然间我想，哦，对了，这就是艺术。

sentences.en: And once I got past that, I started seeing all these quirky, weird little bits.
sentences.zh: 一旦我跨过了那一关，我就开始看到所有这些古怪、奇特的小细节。

sentences.en: And that's when I started thinking, oh, right, these are people just like me who made these.
sentences.zh: 那时我开始想，哦，对了，制作这些的人和我一样也是普通人。

sentences.en: These are people who were being creative, who wanted to be fun, who wanted to enjoy life, even at a moment of terror.
sentences.zh: 这些人富有创造力，想要有趣，想要享受生活，即使在恐怖的时刻也是如此。

sentences.en: Like the women who made this had just lost their country.
sentences.zh: 就像制作这幅挂毯的女性刚刚失去了她们的国家。

sentences.en: They might have even been doing this as forced labor.
sentences.zh: 她们甚至可能是作为强迫劳动力来做这件事的。

sentences.en: They were certainly, you know, probably not doing it that willingly.
sentences.zh: 她们当然，你知道，可能并不是心甘情愿地做这件事。

sentences.en: You know, this was a tapestry of the victor.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一幅胜利者的挂毯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And yet they still managed to get their own personality in to have some fun with it.
sentences.zh: 然而，她们仍然设法融入了自己的个性，并从中获得了一些乐趣。

sentences.en: That's lovely.
sentences.zh: 那太可爱了。

sentences.en: And I thought, this is great.
sentences.zh: 我想，这太棒了。

sentences.en: As you talked with all these people who were there viewing this alongside you, how did all those people that you interviewed, how did they react to seeing the tapestry?
sentences.zh: 当你与所有和你一起参观的人交谈时，你采访的那些人对看到这幅挂毯有什么反应？

sentences.en: What did it mean to them?
sentences.zh: 这对他们意味着什么？

sentences.en: The depth of feeling of this, like just talking to them, just saying, why are you here to see it?
sentences.zh: 这种情感的深度，就像和他们交谈，问他们为什么要来看它？

sentences.en: Yeah, it makes me well up.
sentences.zh: 是的，这让我热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: Why does it make you well up?
sentences.zh: 为什么它让你热泪盈眶？

sentences.en: They were like, this is part of our country.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这是我们国家的一部分。

sentences.en: It goes to the whole core of our history.
sentences.zh: 它触及了我们历史的核心。

sentences.en: It's so vivid.
sentences.zh: 它太生动了。

sentences.en: And as you walk along, you could read the story.
sentences.zh: 当你走过时，你可以读懂这个故事。

sentences.en: This is two men fighting for the future of England.
sentences.zh: 这是两个男人为了英格兰的未来而战。

sentences.en: Happening in front of you, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就在你眼前发生。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Outstanding.
sentences.zh: 杰出。

sentences.en: Beyond expectations.
sentences.zh: 超乎预期。

sentences.en: Absolutely, seriously, outstanding.
sentences.zh: 绝对，真的，太杰出了。

sentences.en: And there was one bizarre moment where a man walked out and told me he was going to get a tattoo.
sentences.zh: 还有一个奇怪的时刻，一个男人走出来告诉我他要去纹身。

sentences.en: And just seeing it in, you know, not the flesh, in the stitch for the first time was absolutely amazing.
sentences.zh: 第一次亲眼看到它，不是实物，而是针脚，真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: You know, I want to get it tattooed on me one day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有一天想把它纹在身上。

sentences.en: And not just any tattoo, but of the most famous scene.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是随便纹个什么，而是最著名的那个场景。

sentences.en: Harold, obviously.
sentences.zh: 当然是哈罗德。

sentences.en: Harold being shot in the eye.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德眼睛中箭的那一幕。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: I reckon him getting shot in the eye would be the one, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想他眼睛中箭的那一幕会是首选，是的。

sentences.en: Alex, how do you make sense of all these folks that you're talking to describing so much meaning being derived from this tapestry?
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，你如何理解你采访的这些人描述从这幅挂毯中获得的如此多的意义？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm thinking about this gentleman who tells you he might get a scene from it tattooed onto his body.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在想那位告诉你他可能会把其中的一个场景纹在身上的绅士。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a depth of feeling you don't expect from embroidery.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是你从刺绣中意想不到的情感深度。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you make sense of this thing doing so much to so many people?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你如何理解这件东西对这么多人产生如此大的影响？

sentences.en: The thing about 1066, the events depicted in this tapestry, is they're both so long ago, such deep history, and in a way, so little understood,
sentences.zh: 关于1066年，也就是这幅挂毯所描绘的事件，关键在于它们既是如此久远的历史，又是如此深奥的往事，在某种程度上，人们对它的了解又如此之少，

sentences.en: that you can read whatever you want into this artifact.
sentences.zh: 以至于你可以对这件文物进行任何你想要的解读。

sentences.en: You know, you can see it as a moment that the country has found it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以把它看作是国家发现自我的时刻。

sentences.en: You can see it as a great celebration of how Britain is filled with people from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它看作是对英国如何汇聚了来自世界各地的人们的一次伟大庆祝。

sentences.en: You can then, if you are anti-migrant, you can see it as a moment Britain is lost, and a testament to that written under duress.
sentences.zh: 然后，如果你是反移民者，你可以把它看作是英国迷失的时刻，以及在胁迫下写下的证明。

sentences.en: You can see it as a great celebration of the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 你也可以把它看作是对君主制的伟大颂扬。

sentences.en: You can see it as an anti-war statement.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它看作是一份反战宣言。

sentences.en: You can see it as a pro-war statement.
sentences.zh: 你也可以把它看作是一份主战宣言。

sentences.en: You can read whatever you want into this.
sentences.zh: 你可以随心所欲地解读它。

sentences.en: You can just see it as an amazing artwork.
sentences.zh: 你也可以仅仅把它看作一件了不起的艺术品。

sentences.en: And I think the fact this tapestry allows everyone to find themselves in it is what gives it its power.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这幅挂毯让每个人都能在其中找到自己的影子，才赋予了它如此强大的力量。

sentences.en: And plus, it is 220 feet long and just so stunningly unique that you're just going to want to celebrate it as soon as you're in a room with it.
sentences.zh: 况且，它长达220英尺，独特得令人惊叹，一旦你置身其中，就会忍不住想要赞美它。

sentences.en: In other words, everyone is projecting onto this tapestry, whatever they want to or need to project onto it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，每个人都在这幅挂毯上投射着他们想要或需要投射的东西。

sentences.en: And that's what all these people in this line have been doing and will continue to do for as long as it's on loan in Britain.
sentences.zh: 而这正是排队的人们一直在做的事情，只要它还在英国展出，他们就会继续这样做。

sentences.en: I wonder, Alex, how your experience at the museum and with the tapestry came to an end.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，我很好奇，你在博物馆和这幅挂毯的参观经历是如何结束的？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, my experience ended, well, like many museum visits do, in the gift shop.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，我的经历和许多博物馆之行一样，最后是在礼品店结束的。

sentences.en: There is bio-tapestry beer, bio-tapestry mead.
sentences.zh: 那里有挂毯主题的啤酒，还有挂毯主题的蜂蜜酒。

sentences.en: I walked around basically a department store's worth of merch.
sentences.zh: 我逛了一圈，简直就像是在逛一家百货商店的周边商品区。

sentences.en: Bio-tapestry bugle, if you ever want to call out orders in military camps or lead a hunting party.
sentences.zh: 还有挂毯主题的军号，如果你想在军营里传令或者带领狩猎队的话，可以用得上。

sentences.en: I wish I could say I resisted.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我能说我抵挡住了诱惑。

sentences.en: Stocks, a chess set for almost just over $1,000.
sentences.zh: 还有棋盘，一套国际象棋要价一千多美元。

sentences.en: I bought a wooden bio-tapestry postcard and sent it to my sister and a bio-tapestry Christmas tree decoration for myself.
sentences.zh: 我买了一张木制的挂毯主题明信片寄给我姐姐，还给自己买了一个挂毯主题的圣诞树装饰品。

sentences.en: My Christmas tree this year is going to have a far too expensive Harold Godwinson being shot in the eye by an arrow.
sentences.zh: 今年我的圣诞树上，将挂着一个价格昂贵得离谱的哈罗德·戈德温森，他的眼睛正被一支箭射中。

sentences.en: As its key decoration.
sentences.zh: 作为它的核心装饰。

sentences.en: I cannot wait to see photos of that Christmas tree.
sentences.zh: 我迫不及待想看到那棵圣诞树的照片了。

sentences.en: Thank you for everything here today, this tour of the tapestry.
sentences.zh: 感谢你今天所做的一切，感谢你带我参观这幅挂毯。

sentences.en: We appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Check your email on Christmas Day.
sentences.zh: 圣诞节那天记得查收邮件。

sentences.en: There'll be a photo there for you.
sentences.zh: 那里会有一张照片给你。

sentences.zh: 本期节目由莉娜·理查兹和蒂娜·安托利尼制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Wendy Doerr and engineered by Sophia Landman.
sentences.zh: 由温迪·多尔剪辑，索菲亚·兰德曼担任录音工程师。

sentences.en: It contains music from Dan Powell and Marion Lozano and has production assistance from Dahlia Haddad.
sentences.zh: 节目包含丹·鲍威尔和马里昂·洛萨诺的音乐，并得到了达莉亚·哈达德的制作协助。

sentences.en: That's it for the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《周日日报》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假日待客指南。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝得烂醉才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
